outcome: Newborn parameters (birth weight, birth length, head circumference, APGAR scores, umbilical cord blood pH)
cohort: The study included data from 15,404 singleton births that occurred between 2009 and 2019 at the public Danube Hospital in Vienna.
finding: Maternal prepregnancy obesity is associated with increased newborn birth length, birth weight, and head circumference, decreased umbilical cord blood pH, higher miscarriage rates, higher preterm birth rates, and higher emergency caesarean section rates.
mod_finding: Obese women experienced a higher rate of emergency caesarean section compared to normal-weight women.
